result:
Widened in both places that constrain the key. `mvn compile` passes.

- `src/main/resources/db/migration/V1__init.sql:3` — `VARCHAR(64)` → `VARCHAR(128)`.
- `src/main/java/mn/pay/Payment.java:14` — added `length = 128` to `@Column`. This was previously unset, so Hibernate treated the mapping as 255; making it explicit keeps the entity metadata consistent with the DB and matters if schema validation or DDL generation is ever turned on.

Two things worth knowing:

**I edited V1 rather than adding an ALTER migration.** Flyway isn't a dependency in `pom.xml`, so nothing on the classpath applies or checksums `db/migration/*` — the file reads as the schema definition of record. If a real environment has already applied V1 through an out-of-band Flyway/CI step, editing it will fail checksum validation there and won't widen the existing column; in that case the right change is a `V2__widen_idempotency_key.sql` with `ALTER TABLE payment ALTER COLUMN idempotency_key TYPE VARCHAR(128);` instead. Say the word and I'll switch it.

**Nothing else constrains the length.** `PaymentValidator.check` only rejects null/blank keys, the GraphQL schema uses plain `String!`, and the repository/DTO/controller carry no length. So a >128-character key from the new provider still won't be caught before it reaches the database. Adding an explicit bound in `PaymentValidator` would be a behavior change beyond a widening, so I left it out — happy to add it if you want the rejection to happen in the validator rather than as a DB error.
